question: A cyclist rides for 2 hours at 15 km/hr and then for 3 hours at 20 km/hr. What is the average speed (in km/hr) of the cyclist for the entire trip?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed is the weighted average of individual speeds using time as the weight.

Average Speed = (S₁ × T₁ + S₂ × T₂) ÷ (T₁ + T₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (15 × 2 + 20 × 3) ÷ (2 + 3)

⇒ Average Speed = (30 + 60) ÷ 5 = 90 ÷ 5 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed 1 (s₁) = 15 km/hr, Time 1 (t₁) = 2 hours

Speed 2 (s₂) = 20 km/hr, Time 2 (t₂) = 3 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 Average Speed = 90 ÷ 5 = 18 km/hr

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered in first part = 15 × 2 = 30 km

⇒ Distance covered in second part = 20 × 3 = 60 km

⇒ Total Distance = 30 + 60 = 90 km

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 3 = 5 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 90 ÷ 5 = 18 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (General Formula)

It is the ratio of total distance travelled to the total time taken for the entire journey. Formula: Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When a person covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is directly given by the formula 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = |x − y|. When they are moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = x + y.
